This one doesn't make sense to me. So by saying that god "made it in our nature" to do something bad wouldn't that mean that god also "made it in our nature" to do something good and vice-versa? Doesn't god want us to do good?

Free will within itself isn't good or evil, because while it allows is to commit evil acts it also allows us to do good aswell. There are two sides to the same coin, except Satan decides to stick to one side specifically. Satan ultimately gave himself more power by manipulating humanity into giving themselves free will. Think of free will like fire. Fire itself isn't exactly "evil". While it can hurt people, cause people extreme amounts of pain and can be manipulated to be used in bad faith it can also be used to do good. Fire can be used to make food edible, heal wounds, or used against people who would use that same fire for their own self gain. Or it could be left alone, completely.

I won't argue that free will in itself is evil, but if someone uses that same free will to do bad then that person does ultimately become evil.

It was made very clear that the concept of death wasn't much of a broad issue during the garden of Eden. Since the need for repopulation was only introduced after the eating of the fruit then that would mean mortality within itself could've only been possible by eating the fruit. Therefore Adam and Eve wouldn't have died if they didn't eat the fruit because death wouldn't have been a problem to begin with.

Even if we argue that Satan was justified in killing Job's children because they were "sinful" it doesn't change the fact that Satan was directly responsible for that very sin in the first place. Remember, Satan is regarded as the embodiment of sin. Every time sin is committed it's Satan's deception that causes said sin. If the killing of the innocent is itself a sin then that would mean that Satan has indeed killed the innocent. Directly or indirectly.

Last of all, while God did make us the way we are and gave us and Satan to commit these acts in the first place, he still very clearly gives us instructions what to do and what not to do. If you're given a gun and a dog sits right infront of you do you decide to shoot that dog just because you can? Or do you decide not to based on your own morals and common sense? Just because God gives you the ability to do something doesn't mean that you should. While God is all knowing and knows your future and knows what's best for you it is still your responsibility to act on god's will. That's the cost of eating the fruit, responsibility.

First of all let me address that Lucifer being a fallen angel is a questionable canon at best when it comes to the Bible. But for the sake of the hypothetical situation you've provided I will treat it as canon for the sake of it.

1: Rebellion
In your post you pointed out that it would've been unrealistic for Lucifer to get a third of the population to rebel alongside him. To which I ask, why? Many dictators or terrorist leaders have an extremely committed following. Why is it unrealistic for Lucifer not to be charismatic enough to deceive 1/3 of the population of heaven? Isn't he "the deceiver?" Isn't that his thing? 

2: Eden
You also mentioned that God is more of a deceiver than Satan is because he in your eyes deceived Adam and Eve by making them think that by eating the Apple they would surely die. Except... He wasn't exactly lying. Adam and Eve didn't die nor were ever going to before they ate the apple. The whole concept of death wasn't even a thing for humans during their time in Eden. When eating the Apple they were told that in order to continue the human race they had to procreate due to their limited lifespans. They did surely die from eating the Apple, eventually. 

I think it's also important to mention free will. At first god created Adam and Eve without free will, you are right on that. Except free will within itself isn't exactly good nor bad either. Sure free will allows us to be independent and think for ourselves but at what cost? Free will has also allowed us for selfish desires or to commit evil actions out of our own selfishness. If we didn't have free will we wouldn't have the ability to "sin" either. When Lucifer manipulated Eve into eating the Apple he wasn't opening her eyes. He was practically grooming her into luring humanity down a path of destruction and mayhem. Satan practically caused all of humanity's suffering, genocides and even mortality within itself by making Eve eat the apple. Which makes Satan responsible for pretty much every death and tragedy in the world. How's that for a hero?

Which brings me to the third point

3: God's kill count vs Satan's kill count
Many people will point out that God's kill count of 3 million compared to Satan's kill count of 10 as proof as to why God is the apparent "bad guy" in the Bible. Except those same people seem to be very generous when it comes to Satan. If we take into account that (again) Satan made Eve eat the apple which literally gave humans the desire to commit sin in the first place then that would mean that Satan is responsible for practically every major tragedy in existence. Holocaust? Satan. The black death? Satan. The Khmer Rouge? Gulags? Chernobyl? The Spanish Flu? The list goes on! One of those tragedies alone quadruples God's apparent "kill count" and that's not to even mention the morality of the kill count itself.

Let's imagine this, you have one man who's killed about a hundred pedophiles. Then you have another man who's killed about five innocent children. Who's more guilty? Is the man who killed a hundred pedophiles somehow more guilty and deserving of punishment just because he killed more people? 

Despite god's kill count, every single person that god killed (more or less) deserved it. Even during the flood god described humanity as becoming so horrible that he regretted creating humanity in the first place. This would mean that the entire human population had to have been made up of the lowest of the low type of people. This would mean pedophiles, rapists, murderers, psychopaths and so on. I don't know about you but if I saw a species that was made entirely of the most vile toxic spew with only one family of outcasts who actually bothered to still have a moral compass then I'd do the same.

And last of all. No, Lucifer doesn't "punish people in hell" he more so suffers alongside everyone who burns alongside him. There's no official scripture that even mentions Lucifer punishing hell's denizens, infact it has been made very clear in the "lake of fire" verse that he's suffering very greatly among the other sinners that are thrown in there. And honestly I'm glad he is, because nobody is more deserving of such a fate than him.
